title: lebih and paling — comparing
pattern: A lebih … daripada / dari B · A paling … · yang paling … · kurang …
explanation: There's no -er or -est in Indonesian: lebih (more) goes before the describing word, and daripada, or dari in speech, brings in the other thing: Bali lebih ramai daripada Lombok, Yang ini lebih murah dari yang tadi. paling is the most: paling enak (the tastiest), and yang paling picks one out: Yang paling murah yang mana? (Which is the cheapest?). In writing ter- does the same job as paling: terbesar, terindah. kurang is less, and it's also the polite way to say not very or not enough: Saya kurang suka pedas (I'm not much of a fan of spicy food), Kopinya kurang manis (The coffee isn't sweet enough).
natural: Choosing and recommending: Mana yang lebih enak? Yang paling dekat di mana? And lebih suka is prefer: Saya lebih suka teh (I prefer tea).
stiff: For one more or some more, Indonesian uses lagi, not lebih: Es tehnya satu lagi (Another iced tea, please). And kurang is gentler than tidak: Saya kurang setuju sounds polite where Saya tidak setuju can sound blunt.

examples.indonesian: Naik ojek lebih cepat daripada naik mobil.
examples.english: Going by ojek is quicker than going by car.

gap.why: Comparing two things with daripada calls for lebih.

examples.indonesian: Kopinya kurang manis. Boleh minta gula?
examples.english: The coffee isn't sweet enough. Could I have some sugar?

gap.why: Not sweet enough is kurang manis; terlalu manis would be too sweet.

examples.indonesian: Menurut Anda, warung mana yang paling enak?
examples.english: Which warung do you think is the best?

gap.why: The best of them all is paling; lebih compares just two.

examples.indonesian: Ini pantai terindah yang pernah saya lihat.
examples.english: This is the most beautiful beach I've ever seen.

gap.why: The most beautiful is ter- + indah, a little more written than paling indah.
